text:
Jim stood in the center of the advanced yoga studio, his face a mask of concentrated effort as he attempted to balance on one leg. The instructor, a serene woman named Serenity, glided past him, whispering, "Find your center, Jim. Let go of the ego."

Jim tried to let go of his ego, but he couldn't let go of the fact that he was wearing his lucky gym shorts, which were slightly too tight. As he twisted his torso into a complex spinal twist, a low, rumbling sound escaped him. It wasn't a chakra alignment; it was a digestive protest.

The class, previously silent and meditative, stiffened. Serenity paused, her eyebrow twitching. "Is that... part of the pose?"

"No," Jim grunted, sweat beading on his forehead. "That's just my body trying to escape."

Just then, the studio door creaked open. A large, long-necked giraffe poked its head in, having mistaken the studio for a buffet. The animal’s presence was so absurdly out of place that the collective zen of the room shattered instantly. The giraffe, seemingly unbothered by the awkward silence, stretched its neck down toward Jim, who was still contorted in a pretzel-like shape.

Jim, terrified and still holding his breath to avoid further bodily betrayals, froze. The giraffe sniffed him, then let out a soft, confused huff. The class erupted into laughter, breaking the tension. Serenity sighed, rubbing her temples. "Well," she said, "at least we're no longer meditating on our chakras. We're meditating on how to get a giraffe out of a yoga studio without causing a scene."

Jim finally exhaled, only to realize he had been holding it for too long. The resulting sound was less of a toot and more of a squeak, like a deflating balloon. The giraffe turned and walked away, clearly unimpressed. Jim collapsed onto his mat, defeated but alive, as the class applauded his unintentional performance art.
